sub.en: Look at the sentences. Which plurals do not end in -s?

items.q: One woman, two ___.
items.why: man → men, woman → women, child → children, person → people. No -s.

___ you from Germany?

items.why: RECYCLED: was/were is the past of am/is/are.

acts.title: One person, four nationalities
text: Godwin is from Nigeria, but he lives in north London. His wife, Sylvie, is French — or half-French: her mother is French and her father is from Brazil.
Their two children were born in England, so they are British. At home the family speaks English, because it is the only language all four of them know.
Their street is very multicultural. The neighbours are a family from Iraq, and next to them there is a Polish shop and a Turkish restaurant.
“People often ask me where I am from,” Godwin says. “It isn’t an easy question. I was Nigerian when I was a child. Now I am a Londoner.”

items.s: The family speaks French at home.
There are people from many countries in their street.

items.q: The word that means “with people from many countries”.
The plural of “person” that Godwin uses.
The plural of “child” in the text.
The nationality word for a person from Britain.

tts: Dubai is a very multicultural city in the United Arab Emirates. People come here to work from many different countries. Only ten per cent of people in Dubai are Emirati: ninety per cent of the city’s population are from other countries. Some people come from the UK and the USA, but many people are from Asia. India is home for most of Dubai’s workers, but people come from Pakistan and the Philippines too. The language of the United Arab Emirates is Arabic.

write.q: Write about three people you know or three famous people: 6 sentences. Say where each is from, their nationality and what languages they speak. Use one plural that does not end in -s.
write.model: My manager is from Brazil. She’s Brazilian, but she lives in Germany now. She speaks four languages: Portuguese, Spanish, German and English. My two children are Kazakh and they speak Kazakh, Russian and a little English. Many people in my street are from other countries — it’s a very multicultural area.

speak.q: Answer out loud: Where are you from? What nationality are you? What languages do you speak? Then say the same about one famous person.
speak.model: I’m from Kazakhstan and I’m Kazakh. I speak Kazakh, Russian and English. Shakira is from Colombia — she’s Colombian and she speaks Spanish, English and Portuguese.
